cost_index_metadata.formula: cost(model, benchmark) = model cost effect * benchmark scale * multiplicative error
cost_index_metadata.row_specific_total_normalization: Reported totals are divided by cost_unit_count when supplied by the adapter.

methodology.capability_index: Capability scores use Epoch AI's Bayesian IRT implementation: a logistic score curve with a beta likelihood, benchmark-specific noise, and hierarchical slope/noise priors. The main index reports posterior means and 90% credible intervals, with every posterior draw calibrated to GPT-4.1 = 100 and GPT-5 = 120. Fits must pass Epoch's convergence checks before publication. Category sub-indices use Epoch's domain-specific method: benchmark parameters are fixed to the main posterior means and model capability is refit by regularized least squares. Their 90% intervals combine 1,000 main posterior draws with ten within-model benchmark bootstrap resamples per draw. Reasoning/context variants are collapsed to a base model key, and each benchmark uses the highest-scoring variant for that base model. Benchmarks with index cutoff bands remain visible in the dashboard, but observations for models released on or after the cutoff are excluded from index fitting and benchmark-count eligibility. The all-benchmark index requires models to appear in at least eight eligible benchmark units and at least one third of eligible benchmark units whose oldest dated model release is on or before the selected model release date, rounded down to the nearest whole number. Category sub-indices use the same one-third category release-date rule and also require the model to appear in at least four benchmarks anywhere in the full eligible index dataset; unlike Epoch's public domain-specific ECI, this dashboard does not require at least two benchmarks within the category. The ECI anchors are declared in capability_index_metadata.
methodology.cost_index: The relative cost index fits log(reported cost) as a model effect plus a benchmark effect after selecting each base model's highest-scoring variant per benchmark. This is equivalent to reported cost = intrinsic model cost multiplier * benchmark scale * multiplicative error. Row-specific totals are divided by their reported run count before fitting. Only positive source-reported costs are used; GPT-4.1 is fixed at 100, and models require cost observations on at least two benchmarks.
methodology.elo_normalization: Elo benchmarks keep raw Elo for display and use expected win probability against the highest-Elo model on that leaderboard divided by 0.5 for normalized scores, capped at 1.0.
methodology.epoch_eci: Epoch ECI scores are loaded from Epoch's public ECI CSV and matched to dashboard model IDs using the same canonical alias rules as benchmark results.
methodology.metr_time_horizon: METR Time Horizon 1.1 is scraped from METR's public YAML and mapped to dashboard model IDs with explicit aliases. Correlations compare capabilities index values to log2 of METR's p50 time horizon in minutes for overlapping models.
methodology.model_normalization: Model labels are cleaned and mapped to stable lowercase IDs; labs are inferred from providers or model-name rules, then enriched from exact model metadata matches and exact canonical aliases.
methodology.parameter_enrichment: Parameters come from Epoch's public model metadata when matched, exact sourced metadata entries for open-weight models, and explicit sizes in model names. Active parameters are included only when sourced or explicit in the model name.
methodology.score_normalization: Percent scores are divided by 100; native 0-1 scores are kept as-is; all scores are clipped to [0, 1]. Lower-is-better benchmarks keep the reported score and invert the normalized score. Benchmarks with declared random baselines are rescaled before capabilities-index fitting so the random baseline maps to 0.
